chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from al-Fadl al-Katib, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when a letter from Abu Muslim came to him. He said: 'There is no answer to your letter. Exit from us.' So we began whispering among ourselves. He said: 'What are you whispering about, O Fadl? Indeed, Allah, Exalted is His Remembrance, does not hasten due to the hastiness of the servants. And removing a mountain from its place is easier than the disappearance of a dominion whose term has not expired.' Then he said: 'So-and-so, son of so-and-so,' until he reached the seventh from the sons of so-and-so. I said: 'So what is the sign between us and you, may I be your ransom?' He said: 'Do not leave the earth, O Fadl, until the Sufyani emerges. So when the Sufyani emerges, answer to us.' He said it three times, and it is inevitable.

key_terms.أَبُو مُسْلِمٍ: Abu Muslim, a prominent general of the Abbasid revolution
key_terms.السُّفْيَانِيُّ: The Sufyani, a specific figure in Shia eschatology who emerges before the reappearance of Imam al-Mahdi
key_terms.زَوَالِ مُلْكٍ: The disappearance/ending of a dominion or government

ai.seo_question: What are the signs and instructions regarding the emergence of the Sufyani and the duration of the current dominion according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the concept of divine timing (ajal) in the transition of power, where Imam al-Sadiq (as) reassures his companion that the fall of the Umayyad/Abbasid dominion is inevitable and cannot be hastened by human effort. It specifically links the end of the current era to the emergence of the Sufyani, a key eschatological figure in Shia tradition, instructing the faithful to remain steadfast until his appearance signals the call to the Imams. This narrative underscores the Shia belief in the preordained nature of history and the patience required during the period of occultation or waiting for the final signs.

en.hubeali: H 14860 – Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al-Husayn, from Abdul Rahmaan Bin Abu Hashim, from Al-Fazl Al-Katib who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdullahasws when a letter of Abu Muslim came to himasws’. So heasws said: ‘There is no answer to your letter. Exit from usasws’. So some of us left the others. Heasws said: ‘Which thing are you walking upon, O Fazl? Allahazwj does not Make Haste due to the hastiness of the servants. And removing a mountain from its place is easier than toppling a government whose term has not ended’. Then said: ‘So and so, son of so and so’ – until heasws reached seven from the sons of so and so’. I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws, so what are the signs with regards to what is in between us and youasws?’ Heasws said: ‘The earth will not depart (end), O Fazl, until the Sufyani comes out. So if the Sufyani comes out, so answer to usasws (to ourasws call)’. And heasws said it thrice: ‘And it is inevitable’.
en.sarwar: 413. Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al-Husayn, from Abdul Rahmaan Bin Abu Hashim, from Al-Fazl Al-Katib who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (a.s.) when a letter of Abu Muslim came to him (a.s.)’. So he (a.s.) said: ‘There is no answer to your letter. Exit from us (a.s.)’. So some of us left the others. He (a.s.) said: ‘Which thing are you walking upon, O Fazl? Allah (azwj) does not Make Haste due to the hastiness of the servants. And removing a mountain from its place is easier than toppling a government whose term has not ended’. Then said: ‘So and so, son of so and so’ – until he (a.s.) reached seven from the sons of so and so’. I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you (a.s.), so what are the signs with regards to what is in between us and you (a.s.)?’ He (a.s.) said: ‘The earth will not depart (end), O Fazl, until the Sufyani comes out. So if the Sufyani comes out, so answer to us (a.s.) (to our (a.s.) call)’. And he (a.s.) said it thrice: ‘And it is inevitable’.
